review_candidates.description: The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD) About Sezzle: With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! Compensation : For this principal development role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD per month, based on experience level and gross amount. This range acknowledges the extensive expertise, leadership capabilities, and significant contributions expected at this level, offering a competitive salary to reflect the value of advanced skills and experience About the Role: We are seeking a hands-on Senior Security Engineer, Network & Zero Trust , to own the network pillar of Sezzle's zero-trust program: every connection explicitly allowed, authenticated by service identity, and attributable after the fact — across our Kubernetes clusters, AWS accounts, and the paths between them. You will take ownership of our network-policy program — default-deny micro-segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters — and carry the rest of the pillar forward with it: identity-aware service-to-service transport, per-application private access, flow-level visibility, and network configuration managed as reviewed code. This is an engineering role: you will write the policies, the tooling, and the rollout automation yourself, and you will carry changes through other teams' services without breaking delivery. You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own the security platform and detection and response, and with the platform and IAM teams on service identity — your network controls are what their work relies on, and your telemetry is what their detections run on. At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we work. In this role you will use and build agentic workflows — flow analysis, policy generation from observed traffic, drift review — that let the team segment a large estate. What You’ll Do: Own east-west segmentation across our Kubernetes clusters: design the segmentation model, derive network policies from observed traffic, and keep every workload reachable only through explicitly allowed, identity-bound paths — a default that holds as the estate grows, not a one-time project. Deliver identity-aware transport — design and roll out mutually authenticated, encrypted service-to-service connections (mTLS), so that authorization decisions rest on verified service identity. Keep a live map of the network: VPC peerings, tunnels, cross-account links, and every public entry point — built from cloud APIs and reconciled continuously, so every path into production is known and justified. Own segmentation of production and the cardholder-data environment: implement and enforce the CDE and high-trust-tier boundaries, review every peering and public exposure against them, and run segmentation testing with the security team. Partner with IT on private access: evaluate and help deliver per-application access (ZTNA) for engineers and operators reaching production systems. Own network telemetry: flow logs east-west and north-south, with enough identity on both ends that "who talked to what, when" is answerable in minutes — and feed it to our SIEM for the detection team. Own cluster admission control and hold the line on drift: workload admission policy (pod security, image provenance, network policy), security groups and firewall rules declared in git, applied only through the IaC pipeline, with admission control at the gate and drift detected and reverted automatically. Contain: build the levers that let us isolate a workload or segment quickly when detection flags lateral movement, and take part in incident response when the network is in play. Participate in threat modeling and design reviews for anything that changes how traffic flows, and in the on-call rotation for the controls you own. What We Look For: 6+ years of experience in security, network, platform, or infrastructure engineering, with hands-on ownership of network controls in cloud production environments. Deep, practical Kubernetes networking knowledge: CNI, NetworkPolicy semantics, DNS, ingress/egress — and experience rolling segmentation out on live clusters without outages. Strong AWS networking: VPCs, subnets, security groups, peering and Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, load balancers, flow logs. Hands-on experience with mTLS and service-to-service authentication (service mesh, proxies, or CNI-level encryption). Infrastructure as code as your default way of working — Terraform and Helm or equivalents, through merge requests and CI, across repositories you don't own. Ability to write real code (Go, Python, or Bash) for tooling and automation, not only configuration. Ability to investigate directly with packet captures, flow logs, and system-level data. Working knowledge of PCI DSS network requirements — segmentation, scoping of the cardholder-data environment, segmentation testing. Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your work today and have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't. Preferred Knowledge and Skills: Cilium / eBPF in production, including Hubble or equivalent flow observability. mTLS at fleet scale, including certificate lifecycle — service mesh (e.g., Istio, Linkerd, Cilium service mesh) and workload identity standards such as SPIFFE/SPIRE. You have built AI-assisted workflows that others adopted — flow analysis, policy generation, drift review. Experience evaluating or deploying ZTNA / identity-aware proxy products. Policy-as-code and admission control (OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, conftest). Experience with network detection — IDS/IPS, anomalous-flow and lateral-movement detection — and with containment during incidents. Familiarity with SOC 2 and with FFIEC-style examination expectations for network security. Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or other regulated environments. About You: You'd rather close a path than document it - an allow-list that exists in production beats a diagram of how the network should look. You change other teams' systems without breaking them - you roll out in observe mode first, measure, and earn the right to enforce. You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. Sezzle’s Technology Stack: Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native Backend: Golang Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes Version Control: Git CI/CD: Gitlab Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying! What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome? At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. #Full-time

review_candidates.description: Role Purpose We are seeking an experienced Senior Database Administrator to take end-to-end ownership of database reliability, availability, performance, security, backup, recovery, and operational standards across Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL environments. This is a hands-on senior role requiring expertise in designing and building database environments from scratch, implementing high availability and disaster recovery, troubleshooting complex production issues, and establishing consistent database operations across projects. The successful candidate will lead database architecture, implementation, monitoring, performance optimization, maintenance, production support, and continuous improvement while working closely with clients, infrastructure teams, application teams, and implementation partners. Key Responsibilities1. SQL Server Architecture and Administration Design, install, configure, patch, upgrade, and maintain enterprise SQL Server environments across on-premises, virtualized, cloud, and hybrid infrastructures. Build database environments from scratch, including instance configuration, storage, service accounts, security, memory, CPU, tempdb, ports, and operational jobs. Design, implement, and troubleshoot Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC) and SQL Server Always On Availability Groups. Manage availability replicas, synchronization modes, quorum, failover policies, listeners, DNS, IPs, subnets, firewall rules, and application connectivity. Design multi-site high-availability and disaster-recovery solutions, including read-only workload routing. Perform database health checks, configuration comparisons, controlled failovers, and DR exercises. 2. Performance Monitoring and Optimization Proactively identify expensive queries, blocking, deadlocks, high CPU/I/O/memory consumption, long-running transactions, and database connectivity issues. Use Query Store, execution plans, Extended Events, DMVs, wait statistics, and diagnostic tools to identify root causes. Troubleshoot cardinality estimation, memory grants, query spills, parallelism, scans, sorts, hash operations, parameter sensitivity, and latch contention. Diagnose tempdb growth, transaction-log pressure, storage bottlenecks, failed jobs, and resource-capacity issues. Optimize queries, indexes, statistics, configuration, and resource allocation in collaboration with application and infrastructure teams. Establish performance baselines and capacity forecasts for CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, logs, backups, and database growth. Address recurring performance issues through permanent corrective actions rather than temporary workarounds such as unnecessary restarts or database shrinking. 3. Indexing, Maintenance and Partitioning Develop and maintain database maintenance jobs for index optimization, statistics updates, integrity checks, backups, cleanup, and reporting. Define workload-specific index rebuild/reorganization and statistics-update strategies. Analyze fragmentation, page splits, index usage, duplicate or overlapping indexes, fill factor, clustering keys, and high-DML workloads. Design and maintain table and index partitioning for large, high-volume databases, including partition functions, schemes, filegroups, and retention policies. Implement sliding-window strategies, partition switching, archival, purging, and partition-level maintenance. Validate partition elimination and assess the impact of maintenance and partition changes on query performance, replication, transaction logs, and availability. 4. Backup, Recovery and Disaster Recovery Design and implement backup and recovery strategies aligned with agreed Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs). Manage full, differential, transaction-log, PostgreSQL physical/logical, and other appropriate backups. Implement encryption, compression, retention, off-site storage, monitoring, alerting, and backup-access controls. Conduct regular restore and point-in-time recovery tests, validate backup integrity and transaction-log chains, and maintain recovery evidence. Develop documented recovery procedures for data corruption, accidental deletion, infrastructure failure, cluster failure, and site-level disasters. 5. PostgreSQL Administration Install, configure, patch, upgrade, and maintain PostgreSQL environments. Build and administer highly available clusters using streaming replication and technologies such as Patroni, etcd/Consul, repmgr, or equivalent solutions. Manage primary/standby nodes, replication slots, WAL, synchronous/asynchronous replication, connection routing, and failover procedures. Implement backup and point-in-time recovery using pgBackRest, Barman, native utilities, or approved enterprise tools. Monitor replication lag, connections, locks, long-running transactions, WAL growth, checkpoints, storage, table/index bloat, and database health. Tune PostgreSQL configuration and queries using pg_stat_statements, EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE, logs, and wait-event analysis. Manage VACUUM, autovacuum, ANALYZE, REINDEX, statistics, permissions, authentication, TLS, certificates, and security hardening. Plan and test failovers, switchovers, recovery procedures, major-version upgrades, and rollback strategies. 6. Security, Replication and Connectivity Establish database security standards covering least-privilege access, role-based permissions, privileged accounts, authentication, auditing, and periodic access reviews. Implement encryption at rest and in transit, certificate lifecycle management, vulnerability remediation, and secure credential/secret management. Configure and troubleshoot SQL Server transactional replication and other approved data-distribution mechanisms. Diagnose replication latency, agent failures, data inconsistencies, transaction-log growth, and subscriber performance. Troubleshoot database logins, drivers, connection strings, DNS, listeners, TLS certificates, firewall rules, and connection pooling. Maintain an inventory of applications, jobs, integrations, monitoring tools, reporting services, and database clients. 7. Technical Leadership and Operational Ownership Act as the senior database authority for clients, infrastructure teams, application teams, vendors, and implementation partners. Define reference architectures and standards for production, non-production, high-availability, and disaster-recovery environments. Review client and partner designs, identify technical risks, and recommend improvements across availability, security, performance, capacity, and recoverability. Lead technical workshops, complex production incidents, root-cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions. Mentor DBAs and support teams, facilitate knowledge transfer, and ensure operational readiness before production go-live. Maintain architecture documents, build guides, configuration baselines, runbooks, health-check reports, recovery procedures, and incident documentation. Required Qualifications and Experience 10+ years of database administration experience, including business-critical production systems. 7+ years of strong, hands-on Microsoft SQL Server administration experience. Proven experience building SQL Server environments from scratch and implementing enterprise high-availability and disaster-recovery solutions. Advanced knowledge of WSFC, Always On Availability Groups, listeners, quorum, multi-node failover, and multi-site architectures. Strong SQL Server performance-tuning expertise covering Query Store, execution plans, DMVs, wait statistics, blocking, deadlocks, indexing, statistics, memory, parallelism, tempdb, and transaction logs. Hands-on experience with enterprise backup, restore, point-in-time recovery, and DR testing. Experience managing large, partitioned, high-DML, and high-transaction-volume databases. Practical PostgreSQL administration experience covering cluster setup, replication, backups, recovery, maintenance, monitoring, security, and performance tuning. Strong T-SQL skills, working knowledge of PostgreSQL SQL, and scripting/automation capabilities. Proven experience working with infrastructure, application, security, DevOps, vendor, and client teams. Ability to lead critical production incidents and communicate technical findings to technical and management stakeholders. Experience preparing architecture documents, implementation guides, operating procedures, health-check reports, and root-cause analyses. Preferred Qualifications Experience in banking, fintech, payments, or other regulated, high-availability environments. Experience supporting geographically distributed production and DR sites. SQL Server transactional replication experience. Exposure to Azure SQL, SQL Server on Azure VMs, or comparable cloud platforms. Familiarity with Redgate, SolarWinds, Dynatrace, SCOM, Grafana/Prometheus, or equivalent monitoring tools. Experience automating database builds, configuration validation, maintenance, and health checks. Relevant Microsoft, PostgreSQL, cloud, or infrastructure certifications. Key Success Measures Database availability and reliability against agreed service targets. Backup success and independently verified restore capability. Compliance with RPO/RTO targets and successful DR/failover exercises. Reduction in recurring incidents, blocking, deadlocks, uncontrolled tempdb growth, and performance issues. Improved critical-query response times and database capacity planning. Healthy SQL Server Availability Groups and PostgreSQL replication. Timely completion of maintenance, patching, certificate renewals, recovery testing, and capacity reviews. Closure of database-readiness risks before production deployment. Consistent adoption of database standards, runbooks, and operational documentation.
